Title: Maturation of medial efferent system function in humans.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults, term and premature neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE primary tones with contralateral broadband noise
Outcome: contralateral suppression present at 1500 and 3000 Hz, absent at 6000 Hz; premature neonates showed suppression or enhancement
Evidence_Quote: at three f2 frequencies: 1500, 3000, and 6000 Hz

Title: Modeling otoacoustic emissions by active nonlinear oscillators.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no subjects (theoretical model; neonatal OAE data used for comparison)
Stimulus_Type: theoretical oscillator models of spontaneous and evoked otoacoustic emissions
Outcome: data incompatible with Van der Pol oscillator; proposed oscillator better reproduces OAE phenomenology
Evidence_Quote: with characteristic damping coefficients in the 20-200 Hz range

Title: Maturation of human fetal responses to airborne sound in low- and high-risk fetuses.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: low- and high-risk preterm fetuses at 27, 30, 33, and 36 weeks GA
Stimulus_Type: airborne sound trials
Outcome: cardiac acceleration and body movement responses began at 30 weeks GA; cardiac threshold decreased with maturation
Evidence_Quote: received three sound trials at 90, 100, 105 and 110 dB

Title: Chronic placental insufficiency has long-term effects on auditory function in the guinea pig.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: guinea pigs (prenatally compromised and controls), tested at 8 weeks of age
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone pips (auditory brainstem responses)
Outcome: no ABR threshold differences; increased wave III latency and I-III interval at high click rates in compromised animals
Evidence_Quote: tone pip stimuli at frequencies of 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 kHz

Title: Chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation in neonatally deafened cats: effects of intensity and stimulating electrode location.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: stimulation at 2 dB above EABR threshold partially prevented spiral ganglion neuron degeneration; effect depended on electrode position
Evidence_Quote: at an extremely low intensity (2 dB above electrically evoked auditory brainstem response threshold)

Title: Cochlear maturation and otoacoustic emissions in preterm infants: a time-frequency approach.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (wavelet time-frequency analysis)
Outcome: CEOAE levels increased and latency decreased with postconceptional age until about 38 weeks, then term-like
Evidence_Quote: decomposed into 12 frequency bands, spanning the 0.25-6.25 kHz range

Title: Characteristics of the audio sound generated by ultrasound imaging systems.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no subjects (theory and water-tank experiments; fetal exposure discussed)
Stimulus_Type: ultrasound imaging pulses (radiation-force generated audio sound)
Outcome: scanner-generated audio sound may reach close to 100 dB in the audible range, suggesting fetal exposure during ultrasound examinations
Evidence_Quote: with a typical spatial-peak pulse-average intensity value at 2 MHz may generate a localized sound-pressure level close to 100 dB

Title: Effects of aspirin on distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression in human adults: a comparison with neonatal data.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human adults (aspirin-induced OHC dysfunction; sensorineural hearing loss) and term newborns
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) ipsilateral suppression
Outcome: aspirin altered suppression at 6000 Hz only; neither aspirin nor SNHL produced neonatal-like suppression
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression was measured at f2 = 1500 and 6000 Hz

Title: Effects of middle-ear immaturity on distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning in infant ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human infants (birth to 6 months) and adults
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE input/output functions and suppression tuning (middle-ear/cochlear model)
Outcome: middle-ear immaturity explained infant-adult DPOAE differences; cochlear mechanics mature at birth
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE suppression tuning at f2= 6000 Hz was similar

Title: Ear asymmetries in middle-ear, cochlear, and brainstem responses in human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: otoacoustic emissions (DPOAE/TEOAE) and auditory brainstem responses
Outcome: right-ear dominance for TEOAE and ABR; no left-ear dominance for DPOAE signal; middle-ear asymmetries did not explain the effects
Evidence_Quote: evaluated separately and across frequencies (1.5, 2, 3, and 4 kHz)

Title: Transient evoked otoacoustic emission latency and estimates of cochlear tuning in preterm neonates.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: transient evoked otoacoustic emissions (latency analysis)
Outcome: latency decreased with postconceptional age only in right ears within the 1.5-2.5 kHz range; tuning estimates decreased
Evidence_Quote: in the 1.5-2.5 kHz frequency range only

Title: Effects of neonatal deafening and chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation on the cochlear nucleus in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn kittens, neonatally deafened, implanted at 10-16 weeks of age
Stimulus_Type: chronic intracochlear electrical stimulation
Outcome: deafening reduced cochlear nucleus spherical cell density, area and volume; chronic stimulation did not reverse these changes
Evidence_Quote: at 6 dB above

Title: Rapid development of a sensory attribute in young chickens.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: background tone frequency changes (habituation, peeping delay)
Outcome: consistent ranking of the frequencies emerged within the first postnatal day
Evidence_Quote: five frequencies between 500 and 608 Hz

Title: Distortion-product otoacoustic-emission suppression tuning in human infants and adults using absorbed sound power.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning curves (absorbed sound power)
Outcome: infant and adult STCs were similar when based on absorbed power; cochlear mechanics substantially mature in full-term infants
Evidence_Quote: occurs at a stimulus frequency of 6 kHz

Title: Developmental changes in ultrasonic vocalizations by infant Japanese echolocating bats, Pipistrellus abramus.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: Japanese house bat (Pipistrellus abramus) pups and adults
Stimulus_Type: natural ultrasonic vocalizations (echolocation precursors and isolation calls)
Outcome: pup vocalizations were frequency-modulated ultrasounds; two call types showed separate developmental patterns
Evidence_Quote: frequency-modulated ultrasounds from 30.0 ± 4.0 kHz to 19.3 ± 1.9 kHz

Title: Postnatal development of 2f1-f2 otoacoustic emissions in pigmented rat.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: distortion-product otoacoustic emissions (primary tones)
Outcome: emissions first detected on postnatal day 14 at 5.7-11.3 kHz; high- to mid-frequency responses matured earlier
Evidence_Quote: The geometric-mean frequencies of the primaries were tested at one-half octave intervals, between 4 and 11.3 kHz

Title: Perception of the pitch of unresolved harmonics by 3- and 7-month-old human infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: unresolved harmonic complexes (missing fundamental), bandpass filtered, with pink noise
Outcome: infants categorized complexes by missing-fundamental pitch, indicating discrimination of unresolved harmonics by 3 months
Evidence_Quote: Stimuli were MF complexes bandpass filtered with a -12 dB/octave slope, combined in random phase, presented at 70 dB sound pressure level (SPL) for 650 ms with a 50 ms rise/fall with a pink noise at 65 dB SPL. The conditions were (1) "LOW" unresolved harmonics (2500-4500 Hz) based on MFs of 160 and 200 Hz and (2) "HIGH" unresolved harmonics (4000-6000 Hz) based on MFs of 190 and 200

Title: Induction of single-sided deafness in the newborn rat and its consequence for cochlear nucleus volume development.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborn rats (operated postnatal day 10), tested as young adults
Stimulus_Type: intracochlear neomycin (single-sided deafness induction); ABR thresholds
Outcome: ventral cochlear nucleus volume on the deaf side was reduced to 57% of the normal-hearing side
Evidence_Quote: Monaural deafening was considered successful when the hearing threshold was at least 95

Title: Heterogeneity of vocal sac inflation patterns in Odorrana tormota plays a role in call diversity.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: natural vocalizations (eight call types), audio/video recording
Outcome: vocal sac inflation pattern depended on call duration and fundamental frequency
Evidence_Quote: those having a fundamental frequency (F0) of >5000 Hz involved inflation of pars lateralis only, whereas those with an F0 of <4000 Hz

Title: Characterizing spontaneous otoacoustic emissions across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: human subjects from premature birth through the seventh decade (632 subjects)
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (no stimulus)
Outcome: newborns had more numerous, higher-level and higher-frequency SOAEs than young adults; elderly ears were reduced in level
Evidence_Quote: Newborn SOAEs are also an average of 5 to 6 dB higher

Title: Music reduces pain perception in healthy newborns: A comparison between different music tracks and recoded heartbeat.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: healthy full-term newborns aged 1 to 3 days
Stimulus_Type: music (Mozart K.448; Beethoven Moonlight Sonata) and recorded heartbeat sounds
Outcome: music and heartbeat exposure reduced heart rate and pain perception and increased oxygen saturation compared with no music
Evidence_Quote: heartbeat sound recordings (70 bpm) or no music

Title: Yes/no and two-interval forced-choice tasks with listener-based vs observer-based responses.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz FM tone in quiet; word in two-talker speech masker
Outcome: observer-based thresholds were higher than listener-based; signal-temporal uncertainty accounted for most of the difference
Evidence_Quote: Detection thresholds were estimated adaptively for a 1000-Hz FM tone

Title: The maturation of the central auditory conduction in preterm infants until three months post term. II. The auditory brainstem responses (ABRs).
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: preterm infants (65 infants, followed to 3 months post term)
Stimulus_Type: auditory brainstem responses (ABR)
Outcome: ABR component detectability reached 80-100% at about 32 weeks conceptional age; latencies decreased with maturation
Evidence_Quote: The detectability of the different components in the ABR tests at 70 dB

Title: Infant speech-sound discrimination testing: effects of stimulus intensity and procedural model on measures of performance.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech sounds /ba/ vs /da/ (operant head-turn procedure)
Outcome: discrimination performance improved significantly with stimulus intensity; response decrement supported a vigilance model
Evidence_Quote: was measured at three stimulus intensity levels (50, 60, and 70 dB SPL)

Title: Auditory brain stem responses from human adults and infants: restriction of frequency contribution by notched-noise masking.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked ABR with notched-noise masking
Outcome: wave V latency and amplitude were similar for adults and infants in the 1.0-kHz notch; differences emerged at higher notch frequencies
Evidence_Quote: Notch center frequencies were set at 1.0, 4.0, and 8.0 kHz. Responses were obtained at 20, 40, and 60 dBnHL

Title: Infants' discrimination of final syllable fundamental frequency in multisyllabic stimuli.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: synthetic multisyllabic speechlike stimuli with final-syllable F0 increments
Outcome: infants discriminated F0 increments of 5-30 Hz above chance; performance did not differ by syllable number
Evidence_Quote: for increments of 10, 20, and 30 Hz relative to a 150-Hz standard

Title: Auditory structure and function in the bird middle ear: an evaluation by SEM and capacitive probe.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: neonatal chick and parakeet (anatomy in five avian species)
Stimulus_Type: acoustic stimulation for tympanic membrane velocity measurement (capacitive probe)
Outcome: tympanic membrane velocity resembled a bandpass filter with best frequency 1.5-3.0 kHz; displacement was linear between 70 and 120 dB SPL
Evidence_Quote: The velocity vs frequency response curve, measured from the tip of the concave tympanic membrane, and corrected to a constant stimulus level of 100 dB SPL, was obtained for the neonatal chick and parakeet for frequencies between 0.2 and 10.0 kHz with a capacitive probe. In both species this curve resembled a bandpass filter whose best frequency was in the range of 1.5-3.0 kHz. The low and high frequency roll-off was 6 and 16 dB per octave, respectively.

Title: Early hearing deprivation by silicon earplugs does not alter electrophysiological development of mouse dorsal cochlear nucleus fusiform neurons.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: early hearing deprivation by silicon earplugs; dorsal cochlear nucleus fusiform neuron electrophysiology
Outcome: fusiform neuron electrophysiological maturation did not differ between earplugged and sham-treated mice
Evidence_Quote: inserting silicon earplugs at P14, elevating auditory thresholds by 30-40 dB

Title: Postpartum survival of mice exposed in utero to ultrasound.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: mice exposed in utero (gestation day 8); neonatal survival assessed
Stimulus_Type: ultrasound exposure (continuous wave, water bath)
Outcome: no credible enhancement of neonatal mortality after in utero ultrasound exposure
Evidence_Quote: to ultrasound at 0.44 W/cm2 (+/- 20%) spatial average intensity, 2 MHz, continuous wave

Title: Fundamental frequency in the speech of infants and children.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: six normal infants and children aged 33 to 169 weeks
Stimulus_Type: speech recordings (narrow-band spectrographic analysis)
Outcome: fundamental frequency values ranged from 30 to 2500 Hz; fry, modal and high registers were discussed
Evidence_Quote: Fundamental frequency values ranged from 30 to 2500 Hz

Title: Acoustic features of infant vocalic utterances at 3, 6, and 9 months.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: infant vocalic utterances (comfort-state recordings)
Outcome: mean f0 was 445 Hz at 3 months, 450 Hz at 6 months and 415 Hz at 9 months; F1 and F2 ranges increased with age
Evidence_Quote: The f0 frequency averaged 445 Hz for 3-month-olds, 450 Hz for 6-month-olds, and 415 Hz for 9-month-olds

Title: Infants require low-frequency energy to hear the pitch of the missing fundamental.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: harmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental)
Outcome: infants categorized low-frequency (resolvable) complexes by missing-fundamental pitch but failed to categorize high-frequency (unresolvable) complexes
Evidence_Quote: based on missing fundamental frequencies of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: The relationship between auditory brainstem response latencies and behavioral thresholds in normal hearing infants and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: tone pips (ABR latencies and behavioral thresholds)
Outcome: 3-month-olds with higher behavioral thresholds had longer wave V latencies and I-V intervals; no such relation at 6 months or in adults
Evidence_Quote: auditory brainstem response (ABR) latencies for 4 and 8 kHz tone pips

Title: Pressure transfer function and absorption cross section from the diffuse field to the human infant ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pink noise in a reverberant diffuse field (ear-canal pressure measurement)
Outcome: ear-canal resonance decreased from 4.4 kHz at 1 month to 2.9 kHz at 24 months; concha resonance decreased from 5.5 to 4.5 kHz
Evidence_Quote: The diffuse-field pressure transfer function from a reverberant field to the ear canal of human infants, ages 1, 3, 6, 12, and 24 months, has been measured from 125-10700 Hz

Title: The growth of hearing loss in neonatal chicks exposed to intense pure tones.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: intense pure tone exposure
Outcome: threshold shift was greatest at 1.3 kHz (maximum loss about 57 dB); tuning sharpness decreased for probe tones above 0.9 kHz
Evidence_Quote: One-day-old chicks were exposed to an intense pure tone (0.9 kHz, 120 dB SPL)

Title: Acoustic impedance of the maternal abdomen.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: nine women in the last trimester of pregnancy
Stimulus_Type: electromechanical shaker (abdominal vibrations)
Outcome: abdominal impedance showed low-frequency compliance, a resonance at 28 ± 16 Hz, and a mass effect at higher frequencies
Evidence_Quote: produced abdominal vibrations between 10 and 500 Hz

Title: Tectorial membrane regeneration in acoustically damaged birds: an immunocytochemical technique.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: octave band noise exposure
Outcome: the tectorial membrane lesion was repaired within 7 days in both chicks and quail
Evidence_Quote: Birds were exposed to an octave band noise with a center frequency of 1.5 kHz at 116 dB SPL for 4 h

Title: Ontogeny of hearing in the marsupial, Monodelphis domestica, as revealed by brainstem auditory evoked potentials.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: brainstem auditory evoked potentials (tone stimuli)
Outcome: hearing onset at postnatal day 29 with range 5-20 kHz; adult audiogram reached by about day 40
Evidence_Quote: The hearing range at the onset of hearing is limited to 5-20 kHz with lowest thresholds of 60 dB SPL at 8-12 kHz

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning curves in human adults and neonates.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 15 normal-hearing adults and 16 healthy term-born neonates
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE (2f1-f2) iso-suppression tuning curves
Outcome: neonatal STCs at 3000 and 6000 Hz were comparable in shape, width and slope to adult STCs; cochlear tuning mature by term birth
Evidence_Quote: The 2f1-f2 DPOAE was elicited using f2/f1 = 1.2, LI = 1.2, LI = 65 and L2 = 50 dB SPL

Title: Anatomy of the normal human cochlear aqueduct with functional implications.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: human temporal bones, ages 0-100 years (101 bones, 19 aged 0-1 years)
Stimulus_Type: anatomical measurements and quantitative modeling of the cochlear aqueduct
Outcome: the aqueduct filters cardiac- and respiration-induced CSF pulses and has little effect on sound transmission above 20 Hz in normal ears
Evidence_Quote: has little effect on normal ossicular transmission of sound for frequencies above 20 Hz. In pathological ears, such as those with ossicular disruption or after a type IV tympanoplasty, a patent aqueduct might affect hearing for frequencies below 150 Hz.

Title: Infants' pitch perception: masking by low- and high-frequency noises.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones and harmonic tonal complexes with low- and high-frequency noise maskers
Outcome: both groups discriminated tones in high-frequency noise but not low-frequency noise; complexes were categorized by missing fundamental in low-frequency noise
Evidence_Quote: Adults and infants were presented with either pure tones of 160 and 200 Hz

Title: Gender distinctions and lateral asymmetry in the low-level auditory brainstem response of the human neonate.
Journal: Hearing research
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone burst stimuli (ABR thresholds)
Outcome: male infants had lower ABR thresholds than females; right-ear wave V amplitude was larger in both sexes
Evidence_Quote: in response to clicks and tone burst stimuli between 500 and 8000 Hz
